items.name: code_executor
items.description: Execute code in an isolated environment with support for Python, JavaScript, and Bash. Uses Docker (network-disabled, read-only, capability-dropped) when the Docker daemon is reachable — this confines the filesystem and network. Without Docker, falls back to a subprocess sandbox that isolates the network and allows writes ONLY inside the working directory: the code starts there, so a relative path reads and writes the files there, while every path outside it is read-only and a write to one fails with a read-only-filesystem error. Reading anywhere the user can read still works, and CPU/process limits are enforced by ulimit, not cgroups. The result reports which backend ran ('sandbox_backend'), whether writes were confined ('filesystem_confined') and the directory writes are allowed in ('writable_root').

global_options.name: --version
global_options.description: show program's version number and exit

global_options.name: --no-animation
global_options.description: Disable live spinners/progress animation (also via NO_COLOR or EFFGEN_NO_ANIM=1)

global_options.name: --theme {default,high-contrast,monochrome,light}
global_options.description: Color theme for terminal output (also via EFFGEN_THEME). high-contrast targets low-vision readers; monochrome keeps structure without hue; NO_COLOR still turns color off entirely

global_options.name: --completion {bash,zsh,fish}
global_options.description: Print shell completion script and exit

serve.name: --host HOST
serve.description: Host to bind to (default 127.0.0.1, loopback-only). Pass --host 0.0.0.0 to expose on all interfaces (set EFFGEN_API_KEY first).

serve.name: --rate-limit N
serve.description: Requests/minute per client IP (overrides EFFGEN_RATE_LIMIT; 0 disables). Health probes are always exempt.

serve.name: --trust-proxy
serve.description: Trust the first X-Forwarded-For hop as the rate-limit client IP (overrides EFFGEN_TRUST_PROXY). Enable only behind a reverse proxy that sets/overwrites this header — otherwise any caller can spoof it to bypass the rate limit.

models browse.name: --search TEXT
models browse.description: Case-insensitive substring match on model id, family, or provider

models browse.name: --min-context N
models browse.description: Only models with a context window of at least N tokens

models browse.name: --max-price-in USD
models browse.description: Only models whose input price ($/1M) is at most USD

models browse.name: --max-price-out USD
models browse.description: Only models whose output price ($/1M) is at most USD

models browse.name: --include-local
models browse.description: Also list models downloaded in the local HuggingFace cache

models list.name: --provider PROVIDER
models list.description: Show only this provider's models (full detail)

eval.name: --suite SUITE
eval.description: Built-in suite name (math, tool_use, reasoning, safety, conversation) OR a path to your own .jsonl/.json test cases

eval.name: --provider PROVIDER
eval.description: Provider for a bare model id (e.g. openai, groq, cerebras, gemini, together, fireworks, replicate, anthropic, hf). Equivalent to the "provider:model" prefix.

eval.name: --threshold THRESHOLD
eval.description: Per-case pass score for continuous scoring modes (semantic_similarity, llm_judge); has no effect on exact_match/contains/regex, whose scores are already binary (0 or 1) (default: 0.5). Use --fail-under to gate the exit code on suite accuracy.

eval.name: --fail-under ACCURACY
eval.description: Minimum suite accuracy required for a zero exit code (default: 0.5). This is the CI gate; a --compare- baseline regression always fails regardless of this value.

eval.name: --temperature TEMPERATURE
eval.description: Sampling temperature for the evaluated agent (0 for deterministic, reproducible scoring where the provider supports it; default: the model/preset default)

eval.name: --baseline-dir DIR
eval.description: Directory for --save-baseline/--compare-baseline files (default: ./.effgen/baselines under the current directory, created if missing). A baseline saved under the installed package tree by an older effGen version is still read.

eval.name: -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
eval.description: Output file for results. The extension chooses the format: .html renders the shareable report, .md writes Markdown, anything else writes JSON.

eval.name: --report PATH.html
eval.description: Write a self-contained HTML report to PATH — pass rate, exit gate, by-difficulty breakdown, and every case. The file opens offline with no external references.

eval.name: --max-cases MAX_CASES
eval.description: Only run the first N cases (quick subsample)

eval.name: --json
eval.description: Emit the results object as JSON to stdout (for CI gating)

eval.name: --no-animation
eval.description: Disable the live progress bar (plain output)

compare.name: -m MODELS, --models MODELS
compare.description: Comma-separated model ids. Use a provider:model prefix to pin a provider for a bare id (e.g. groq:llama-3.1-8b-instant,gpt-5-nano).

compare.name: --suite SUITE
compare.description: Built-in suite name (math, tool_use, reasoning, safety, conversation) OR a path to your own .jsonl/.json test cases

compare.name: --threshold THRESHOLD
compare.description: Per-case pass score for continuous scoring modes (semantic_similarity, llm_judge); has no effect on exact_match/contains/regex, whose scores are already binary (0 or 1) (default: 0.5). compare always exits 0 — it reports a bake-off rather than gating a build; use `eval --fail-under` for CI gating.

compare.name: --temperature TEMPERATURE
compare.description: Sampling temperature for every compared model (0 for deterministic, reproducible scoring where the provider supports it; default: the model/preset default)

compare.name: --provider PROVIDER
compare.description: Provider applied to any bare model id in --models that has no "provider:" prefix of its own (e.g. openai, groq, cerebras, gemini, together, fireworks, replicate, anthropic, hf).

compare.name: --max-cases MAX_CASES
compare.description: Only run the first N cases (quick bake-off on a big suite)

compare.name: -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
compare.description: Output file for results. The extension chooses the format: .html renders the shareable report, .md writes Markdown, anything else writes JSON.

compare.name: --report PATH.html
compare.description: Write a self-contained HTML report to PATH — the recommended model and why, a per-model table, and accuracy/cost/latency charts. The file opens offline with no external references.

compare.name: --json
compare.description: Emit the comparison matrix as JSON to stdout (for CI gating)

compare.name: --optimize {accuracy,cost,latency}
compare.description: What the recommendation optimizes for (default: accuracy — highest accuracy, tie-broken on lower latency then fewer tokens). 'cost'/'latency' recommend the cheapest/fastest model among those meeting --threshold accuracy (falling back to the full field if none qualify), tie-broken on higher accuracy.

compare.name: --no-animation
compare.description: Disable the live progress bar (plain output)

compare.name: --judge MODEL
compare.description: Model that grades answers under --scoring llm_judge. Without it each model grades its own answers; naming a judge has one model grade the whole field. The judge is named in the output.

battle.name: -m A,B[,C], --models A,B[,C]
battle.description: Comma-separated model ids to race (at least two), e.g. openai:gpt-5-nano,groq:llama-3.1-8b-instant

battle.name: --judge MODEL
battle.description: Model asked to pick the best answer. Optional — the measured outcomes need no judge.

battle.name: --temperature TEMPERATURE
battle.description: Sampling temperature applied to every model

battle.name: --max-tokens MAX_TOKENS
battle.description: Output token cap applied to every model

battle.name: --system-prompt TEXT
battle.description: System prompt applied to every model

battle.name: -o PATH, --output PATH
battle.description: Save the battle. The extension chooses the format: .md writes Markdown, anything else writes JSON.

battle.name: --report PATH.html
battle.description: Write a self-contained HTML report of the battle

battle.name: --json
battle.description: Print the battle as JSON to stdout (no live view)

battle.name: --no-animation
battle.description: Skip the live side-by-side view and print the result

cost.name: -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
cost.description: Output file for the spend summary. The extension chooses the format: .html renders the shareable report, anything else writes JSON.

cost.name: --report PATH.html
cost.description: Write a self-contained HTML spend report to PATH — total against the daily budget, a per-provider/model table, and cost-share charts. The file opens offline with no external references.

loadtest.name: --scenario {fixed,synthetic,multi_tool}, -s {fixed,synthetic,multi_tool}
loadtest.description: Workload scenario: fixed | synthetic | multi_tool (default: fixed)

loadtest.name: --ramp-up SECONDS
loadtest.description: Ramp-up period: stagger VU starts over N seconds (default: 0)

loadtest.name: --think-time SECONDS
loadtest.description: Simulated think-time between requests per VU (default: 0)

loadtest.name: --provider NAME
loadtest.description: Provider for live runs (e.g. cerebras, openai). Default: mock

loadtest.name: -m MODEL_ID, --model MODEL_ID
loadtest.description: Model id for live runs. With --provider, a bare id (e.g. gpt-oss-120b); with --url, the full id the server expects (e.g. openai:gpt-5-nano). Default: mock

loadtest.name: --url URL, --target-url URL
loadtest.description: Base URL of a running `effgen serve` instance (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8000). When set, the load test drives POST {URL}/v1/chat/completions over HTTP -- exercising auth, rate limiting, and the rest of the middleware stack -- instead of calling a provider adapter directly. Requires --model. Mutually exclusive with --provider.

loadtest.name: --api-key KEY
loadtest.description: Bearer token for --url mode. Defaults to $EFFGEN_API_KEY if unset.

loadtest.name: --output PATH, -o PATH
loadtest.description: Write the report to PATH. The extension chooses the format: .html renders the self-contained HTML report, anything else writes JSON. If omitted, the report is only printed to stdout.

loadtest.name: --report PATH.html
loadtest.description: Write a self-contained HTML report to PATH — latency percentiles, throughput, error rate, and the error breakdown. The file opens offline with no external references.

serve_env.name: EFFGEN_API_KEY
serve_env.description: static API key (Bearer or X-API-Key). If unset and not in dev mode, an ephemeral key is minted and printed once — never unauthenticated.

serve_env.name: EFFGEN_DEV_MODE=1
serve_env.description: disable auth (loud warning; local dev only).

serve_env.name: EFFGEN_RATE_LIMIT
serve_env.description: requests/minute per client IP (0 disables; health probes are always exempt). Or use --rate-limit.

serve_env.name: EFFGEN_TRUST_PROXY=1
serve_env.description: trust the first X-Forwarded-For hop as the rate-limit client IP (default: off — the raw socket peer is used, since a caller can set that header to anything). Enable only behind a reverse proxy that sets/overwrites it.

serve_env.name: EFFGEN_CORS_ORIGINS
serve_env.description: comma-separated allowed origins (default: none; cross-origin is fail-closed for a backend API).

serve_env.name: EFFGEN_OIDC_ISSUER / EFFGEN_OIDC_CLIENT_ID
serve_env.description: enable OIDC/JWT auth instead of a static key.

serve_env.name: EFFGEN_PUBLIC_DASHBOARD=1
serve_env.description: serve /dashboard/data.json + /dashboard/spans without auth, for local viewing (default: auth; the /dashboard page itself always loads, but its data calls 401 without this or an API key).

serve_env.name: EFFGEN_NO_DOTENV=1
serve_env.description: skip the .env filesystem search entirely, so only environment variables the orchestrator set are visible (EFFGEN_DOTENV=none is equivalent).

options.name: -p [TASK], --print [TASK]
options.description: Run one task and print the result. Takes the task directly, or reads it from stdin when given alone.

options.name: -m MODEL, --model MODEL
options.description: Model to use

options.name: --provider PROVIDER
options.description: Provider for a bare model id (e.g. openai, groq, cerebras, gemini, together, fireworks, replicate, anthropic, hf). Equivalent to the "provider:model" prefix.

options.name: -w DIR, --workspace DIR
options.description: Directory the agent reads and writes (created if missing). Sets EFFGEN_WORKSPACE for the run; nothing outside it is written.

options.name: --plan
options.description: Propose the change without writing a file or running a command

options.name: --auto-edit
options.description: Apply file writes and sandboxed runs without asking; shell commands still need confirmation

options.name: -y, --yes
options.description: Apply writes, sandboxed runs and shell commands without asking (still confined to the workspace)

options.name: --review [TARGET]
options.description: Review instead of change: read-only, with no tool that writes a file or runs a command. TARGET is uncommitted (the default), staged, or any revision or range git accepts (HEAD~3, main...HEAD). Combine with -f/--file, or use -f/--file alone to review files outside a repository.

options.name: -f PATH, --file PATH
options.description: Include a workspace file in the review, in full. Repeatable. Used with --review, or on its own to review files without a diff.

options.name: --session-id ID, --resume ID
options.description: Continue a persistent session by id (the same store as `effgen chat --session-id` and `effgen sessions list`). Prior turns are recalled and new ones saved, along with the workspace, files in context and files written; a new id starts a fresh session.

options.name: --commit
options.description: After the run, offer to commit the files it wrote (y/N; needs --yes without a terminal). Only those files are committed, and it never pushes, amends, resets or discards your work.

options.name: --commit-message MSG
options.description: Commit message for --commit (default: a message naming the changed files and the task)

options.name: --undo
options.description: Reverse the last applied edit(s) in the workspace instead of running a task, restoring the previous file content

options.name: --undo-count N
options.description: With --undo, how many recent edits to reverse (default 1)

options.name: --max-iterations MAX_ITERATIONS
options.description: Iteration cap for the plan/run/fix loop (default: the coding preset's)

options.name: --temperature TEMPERATURE
options.description: Temperature

options.name: --max-tokens MAX_TOKENS
options.description: Max output tokens per call (raise for reasoning models that spend part of the budget before any visible text)

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the result as one JSON document on stdout (answer, files_written, diffs, actions, tokens, cost). Human output goes to stderr.

options.name: -v, --verbose
options.description: Verbose output (show DEBUG/INFO logs)

options.name: -q, --quiet
options.description: Quiet output (answer only)

options.name: --no-animation
options.description: Disable live spinners/progress animation

slash_commands.summary: Apply the staged edits:  /apply [n]  (n = one edit by number)

slash_commands.name: /reject

slash_commands.name: /undo
slash_commands.summary: Reverse the last applied edit(s):  /undo [n]

slash_commands.name: /drop

slash_commands.name: /model

slash_commands.name: /cost

slash_commands.name: /trace

slash_commands.name: /reset

slash_commands.summary: Load a saved coding session:  /load [name|number]

middleware_hooks.what: Called once after the run finishes. Return the response to report.

middleware_hooks.what: Called after each generation. Return the result to use.

middleware_hooks.name: after_tool_call
middleware_hooks.what: Called after each tool dispatch. Return the output to use.

middleware_shipped.what: Log every model call and tool call the run makes.

middleware_shipped.what: Ask before letting named tools run.

compaction.name: SummarizeOldest
compaction.what: Summarize everything but the most recent few. The default.

compaction.name: DropOldest
compaction.what: Discard the oldest messages without summarizing them.

compaction.name: KeepFirstAndLast
compaction.what: Keep the opening turns and the recent ones; compact the middle.

compaction.name: KeepToolResults
compaction.what: Drop the reasoning, keep what the tools returned.

checkpoint_stores.what: A checkpoint store backed by one JSON file per run.

checkpoint_stores.what: A checkpoint store that lives and dies with the process.
